Statement
Recommendations on Restructuring of SAI Promotional Schemes
- B.V.P. Rao Committee Report
After examining the Schemes and constraints faced in their effective implementation, 
the Committee submits the following recommendations:– 
1. National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC)  – The Committee reviewed the 
scheme started in 1985 and found that it could not produce desirable results 
essentially because SAI does not have direct control over the training and 
management of Athlete. Another reason is education system predominantly 
focused on academics neglecting sports. The committee feels that any result 
in sports excellence from school system can only come from the education 
policy and to encourage for sports excellence as part of education. The glaring 
example in this context is SAI’s adoption of 49 Navodaya Vidyalaya and 
thereafter dropping of the school from the programme. As a matter of fact 
the Navodaya Vidyalayas which were directly under the control of Education 
department of HRD Ministry, Government of India couldn’t coordinate with 
SAI and Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to produce desired results. 
Hence, the Committee recommends closing of NSTC. 
 The Committee also feels that the Ministry of Youth Affair and Sports 
(MYAS) should take up with the HRD Ministry to include sports excellence 
as part of education in Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalays and others. 
On the other hand MYAS should also take up with the State Government 
to include sports excellence to their sports curriculum. 
 The Committee is of the opinion that atleast 1% of both union budget and 
budget of the States should be allotted for sports, so that there is enough 
inputs for sports development at grass-root levels. 
2. The recommendations of dropping of NSTC and retention of SAG and 
ABSC and establishing Sports Academies is based on the belief that grass 
root sports development should be integral part of education system by 
union and State Governments and top sports excellence should be managed 
by SAI and MYAS.

1124 Written Ans. to Std. and [RAJYA SABHA] Ustd. Ques.  of 29 July, 2015
3.  The Committee finds that Army Boys Sports Company (ABSC) is doing well. 
Though there are some problems, the scheme has produced valuable results. 
Hence the Committee recommends the continuation and further expansion 
of ABSC Centres from 18 to 50 by extending it to Navy and paramilitary 
forces also. 
4.  SAI Training Centre (STC)/Centre of Excellence (COE)/Academies-The existing 
STCs/COEs were reviewed and found that these Centres can be converted 
into Sports Academies. Currently there are 56 STCs and 15 Centre of 
Excellence [COE] functioning across the country. The Committee finds that 
SAI should convert the present infrastructure of STCs and COEs into SAI 
Sports Academies. A total of 200 SAI Sports Academies in various States 
are recommended. 
5.  Special Area Game (SAG) Schemes are aimed to tap and nurture the natural 
sports talent available in abundance in remote tribal, rural, coastal and hilly 
areas. Inspite of the change in induction process of SAG and gross neglect 
of the management of the Centres, the scheme has produced commendable 
results. Hence, the committee recommends the continuation and expansion 
of scheme and increase the number of Centres from 19 to 30. 
6. The committee also reviewed the structure and functions of SAI Regional 
Centres and Academic Institutions. It is recommended that 50 National Sports 
Academies covering all summer and Winter Olympic Sports disciplines, Asian 
and Commonwealth Games disciplines and Paralympics Sports disciplines. 
The Committee prefers single sport national academies. However to use the 
existing infrastructure and staff at the SAI regional Centres and academic 
institutions, multi-disciplinary (not more than 3 disciplines) SAI Sports 
academies may be established. 
7. To reorganize SAI Schemes on the above lines of the Committee 
recommendations, immediate recruitment of Assistant Directors and coaches 
as given in the report, should be undertaken. 
8. Extension Centre Scheme may be retained and renamed Sports Outreach 
Scheme. 
Recommendations on Indigenous Games and Martial Arts (IGMA)
1. No further expansion of NSTC scheme, so that sports gets integrated with 
education. Therefore it is recommended to approach HRD and Education 
Ministry to restructure its policy, in order to direct the State Governments 
to emphasize mainly on the sports in education. 

Written Ans. to Std. and  [30 July, 2015] Ustd. Ques.  of 29 July, 2015  1125
2. Coaches who are presently working in the scheme to be redeployed in other 
schemes of SAI. 
3. Since schooling education primarily lies with the State bodies, the NSTC 
has to be executed at the State level. 
4. NSTC mainly promotes the broad basing of sports; hence it is recommended 
that this scheme is executed at State level and not at Centre. On the other 
hand, SAI’s main objective is excellence, which on theoretical sporting model 
would be one-step higher than broad-basing. 
5. Indigenous Games and Martial Arts [IGMA] and Akharas Schemes will be 
revamped and form a feeder Centers to SAG and SAI Sports Academies. 
Recommendations on Army Boys School Company (ABSC)  
Continuation of the scheme by improving various aspects of the Scheme as follows:
1. Committee feels that current number of 18 to be increased to 50 to have 
one company each in regimental centre of the Army. It was also felt that 
similar fashion of Boys Sports Company to be introduced in Navy and 
Paramilitary Forces. 
2. Hence Committee feels total number of Boys Sports Company may go upto 
50 in next five years. 
Recommendations on SAI Training Centres (STC)  
1. SAI Training Centre (STC)/Centre of Excellence (COE)/Academies-The existing 
STCs/COEs were reviewed and found that these Centres can be converted 
into Sports Academies. 
2. Currently there are 56 STCs and 70 No of Extension Centres functioning 
across the country. 
3. The committee finds that SAI should convert the present infrastructure of 
STCs and COEs into SAI Sports Academies. 
4.  A total of 200 SAI Sports Academies in various States are recommended. 
Recommendations on Special Area Games (SAG)  
1. Hence, the Committee recommends continuance of the scheme in its existing 
form as a distinct Scheme separate from the STC Scheme, keeping its USP 
intact undiluted and undisturbed. 
2. There is, however, an urgent need for improving and modernizing the 
infrastructure facilities under this scheme for which adequate provision 
needs to be made at the earliest on the same lines as that of the STCs for 

1126 Written Ans. to Std. and [RAJYA SABHA] Ustd. Ques.  of 29 July, 2015
development of infrastructure, replacement of obsolete equipment including 
office equipments furniture fixtures etc.
3. The basic concept of the scheme of scouting natural talent from tribal, rural, 
coastal and hilly areas and also from the regions/ communities, which are 
genetically and geographically advantageous in particular sports disciplines, 
should not be compromised with. The SAG Centres, which do not fall under 
the above criteria, strictly, should be re-named as SAI Sports Academy Centres 
and all provisions should apply thereto. In case, there is no performance, 
the same should be discontinued. 
4. It is recommended that the number of SAG Centres may be enhanced 
from present 19 Centres to at least 30 SAG Centres in next five years. It 
is recommended that Assistant Director/Deputy Director must head all SAG 
Centres with proper periodical monitoring and evaluation mechanism in place. 
Four to five Coaches for each SAG Centre based on the sports disciplines 
and number of events may be posted along with support staff. The detailed 
staffing pattern is given in the Annexure 1. 
5. Special Area Games Centre set up to tap the natural talent among Siddi 
tribe of negroid origin at North Karwar (Karnataka) and Gir (Gujarat) were 
discontinued in spite of giving best results at National and International 
Events. It is recommended that the two Siddi SAG Centres at North Karwar 
(Karnataka) and Gir (Gujarat) may be restored immediately. 
6. A SAG football Centre may be established to pull up the Junior Talent of 
the entire North East in one place preferably at Shillong immediately to 
channelize the north east talents for Indian Jr. Team for Youth World Cup 
(U-17) to be held in India. This Centre may be setup at SAG, NEHU, 
Shillong. 
7. A Committee may be constituted to identify regions to set up new SAI 
SAG Centres. The same Committee to assess the present status of SAG 
Centres and recommend for rationalisation of sports disciplines, renovation, 
up-gradation and addition of Sports infrastructure including training facilities. 
8. The details of strengthening of Special Area Games highlighting the need for 
restoring the selection procedure, staffing pattern, rationalization of disciplines 
in the existing SAG Centres and the list of Indigenous Games and Martial 
Arts which form of the main source for selection under SAG Centre is 
placed at Annexure 1. 
9. It is also recommended that SAI should arrange competent foreign coaches 
in games like Archery, Fencing, Wrestling, Boxing, Water Sports etc. to 

Written Ans. to Std. and  [30 July, 2015] Ustd. Ques.  of 29 July, 2015  1127
further enhance the genetic advantage of hilly/ tribal sports persons where 
India is making a mark at various International events, thereby reducing 
the time span normally required to achieve medals at major international 
competitions like Olympics/Asian Games/World Championship etc. 
Recommendations on Extension Centres of STC or SAG 
1. To rename the scheme as Sports Outreach Scheme (SOS) which has been 
designed to cater to schools, colleges and Universities across India 
2. It is advised to thoroughly review the existing Extension Centres and continue/
discontinue as per review report. 
3. It is recommended to operate SOS only at Non-Residential facilities. 
4. It is also recommended that the scheme should operate only up to 2 disciplines 
at each Centre. 
5. 250 Centres to be added under the scheme in a phased manner in next 5 
years. 
6. Proper selection should be made so that the best Schools/Colleges in terms 
of sports achievement/playing facilities are adopted. 
Recommendations on National Sports Academies (NSA) 
1. 50 National Sports Academies to cover all Summer Olympics Sports, Winter 
Olympic Sports, Asian and Commonwealth Games disciplines and Paralympics 
Sports. 
2. To begin with, it is recommended to establish National Sports Academies 
at existing Regional Centres of SAI/Academic Institution. 
3. Identification of locations for setting up National Academies other than the 
infrastructure of SAI regional Centre/institutes. 
4. To start 4 years (3+1) academic courses in the academies to be established 
in regional Centres, which have requisite faculty, infrastructure including

Lack of infrastructure for football
1117. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that lack of infrastructure is hampering Indian football; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps to be taken to improve the infrastructure 
in future?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS (SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL): (a) and (b) Sir, sports infrastructure 
for football is already available in the country, which is augmented/upgraded on a 
continuing basis.  
‘Sports’ is a State subject and it is primarily the responsibility of the 
State Governments to create adequate sports infrastructure, including that for  
football, within the States. The Ministry supplements the efforts of the State 
Governments in creation/development of sports infrastructure, including that for 
football in States.  
The Ministry’s Scheme of Rajiv Gandhi Khel Abhiyan (RGKA) provides for 
construction of Integrated Sports Complexes, both for outdoor and indoor sports 
disciplines, in all block panchayats of the country in a phased manner. Football is 
included in the list of outdoor sports disciplines for Integrates Sports Complexes to 
be created/developed at block panchayats under RGKA. 
Further, the Ministry’s Urban Sports Infrastructure Scheme (USIS) provides for 
financial assistance for creation/development of football grounds also.  

Written Ans. to Std. and  [30 July, 2015] Ustd. Ques.  of 29 July, 2015  1129
As India is hosting the FIFA Under 17 Football World Cup in 2017, football 
grounds/stadia in States, where football matches will be played, will also be upgraded/
renovated. Central Government has already approved ` 95 crore for upgradation of 
football stadia for the FIFA Under-17 World Cup Football, 2017. 
Contributions received by NSDF
1118. SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL DARDA: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry is administering National Sports Development Fund 
(NSDF) for the promotion of sports in the country; 
(b) if so, how much contribution it has received from various organizations since 
its inception, and contribution made organization-wise; 
(c) whether Government has provided matching grant to the NSDF accordingly;
(d) what are the reasons that banks/PSUs and other private organizations have 
not been contributing to this fund; and 
(e) how this fund has been utilized by the Ministry so far?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS (SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL): (a) The National Sports Development 
Fund (NSDF) was established under Charitable Endowments Act vide Government 
of India Notification dated 12.11.1998 with the object of promotion of sports and 
games in the country.
(b) and (c) The information is given in Statement ( See below).
(d)  Many entities in the corporate sector may have their own projects/Schemes 
for extending support for social causes including promotion of sports. Corporate sector 
has been encouraged to contribute to NSDF for promotion of sports and games in 
the country; such contribution is 100% tax exempt. Also, efforts to create awareness 
about NSDF have been intensified.
(e) Top level Indian sportspersons, who are medal winning prospects in Olympics 
are under the newly formulated programme namely, ‘Target Olympic Podium (TOP) 
Scheme’ to enhance the medal winning prospect for Olympic Games 2016 and 2020. 
The assistance is given for their customized training both in India and abroad, to 
prepare them for winning medals at international levels. The athletes are selected 
based on their performance and future potential.
Reputed organizations/institutes, engaged in promotion of sports activities, can 
also get financial assistance for specific projects for sports promotion like creation 
of infrastructure, procurement of equipment etc.

Formulation of new National Sports Talent Search Scheme
1120. SHRI A. U. SINGH DEO: 
 SHRI RA VI PRAKASH VERMA:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government has formulated and communicated a new 
National Sports Talent Search Scheme to State Governments/UTs; 
(b) if so, the details in this regard and salient features of the said scheme; 
(c) the details of funds allocated for the said scheme during 2015-16 and the 
details of funds released and actual expenditure so far incurred by various States; 
(d) the details of the criteria fixed for allocation of funds to States; and 
(e) the extent to which the scheme has been able to achieve its objectives in 
the first six months of its introduction in various States?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS (SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL): (a) and (b)  Yes Sir. The Ministry of 
Youth Affairs and Sports has formulated a new National Sports Talent Search Scheme 
(NSTSS), through which talented sportspersons will be identified and nurtured so as 
to enable them to participate in National and International Sports events, win medals 
and bring laurels to the country. The guidelines for implementation of the Scheme 
have been issued to all States/UTs on 20.02.2015. Salient features of the Scheme 
are given in the Statement–I ( See below). 
(c) The Scheme is proposed to be implemented from the current financial year 
(2015-16). No funds have been released under the Scheme so far. 
(d) and (e) The details of criteria fixed for allocation of funds to States is given 
in the Statement–II ( See below). Since the Scheme is proposed to be implemented 
from the current financial year and is yet to be introduced in the States/UTs, no 
achievement has been made so far under the Scheme.

1244 Written Ans. to Std. and [RAJYA SABHA] Ustd. Ques.  of 29 July, 2015
Statement-I
Salient features of National Sports Talent Search Scheme (NSTSS)
 ● Identification of Sporting Talent amongst children (Both Boys and Girls) in 
the age group of 8-12 in Schools all over the country by conducting battery 
of 6 tests at each selection level on students in each School.  
 ● 4 boys and 4 girls securing the total highest marks will be shortlisted from 
each school for Block level tests.
 ● 16 boys and 16 girls securing highest total marks at Block level tests will 
be shortlisted for the District level tests. 
 ● The total marks obtained at District level tests by each of these 32 students 
per block will be compiled and a common merit list prepared. 
 ● Out of this combined merit list the top 1000 boys and 1000 girls from 
different districts securing highest total marks will be shortlisted from each 
State. 
 ● Admission in the State Sports Schools/Central Sports Schools/Junior Sports 
Academies/State Sports Academies/State Sports Hostels etc., and benefit 
under various other State Sports Schemes will be done from this list of boys 
and girls having sports talent/potential and identified through the NSTSS.
 ● Besides, high performing candidates of 8-12 age group in RGKA Rural 
Competitions will also be eligible for admission in the State Sports Schools 
etc., mentioned above. 
 ● The total estimated expenditure for 5 years will be around ` 210 crore.
